speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg. To better understand what is going on, can you tell me how long this lesion has been present and if it started as a blister or a bump?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease, diabetes, and recent steroid use for uveitis, are you currently taking any immunosuppressive medications, and have you noticed any fever or fatigue alongside this leg lesion? REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, CRP, and ESR; REQUEST TEST: TST or IGRA for Tuberculosis.
